blocks.text: Halogenoalkanes are very useful in daily life, largely because of their chemical stability. Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) were once used as refrigerants and aerosol propellants, though they are being replaced because they damage the ozone layer. In medicine, halogenated compounds are powerful anaesthetics, and halogenoalkanes are important intermediates in making polymers such as PVC (polyvinyl chloride) for pipes and PTFE (Teflon) for non-stick cookware.

Halothane, CF3-CHClBr, is a halogenated hydrocarbon widely used as a powerful inhaled anaesthetic: it causes a reversible loss of consciousness during surgery. Chloroform and other chlorinated anaesthetics used earlier are no longer used because of their toxicity.

blocks.title: Halogenoalkane
blocks.text: A halogenoalkane forms when one or more hydrogen atoms of an alkane are replaced by halogen atoms (X = F, Cl, Br or I). With one, two, three or more halogen atoms it is a mono-, di-, tri- or polyhalogenoalkane. Monohalogenoalkanes are also called alkyl halides, R-X.

items: Primary: the carbon carrying X is joined to one or no other carbon atom, e.g. chloromethane CH3Cl, chloroethane CH3CH2Cl, 1-chloropropane CH3CH2CH2Cl.
Secondary: the carbon carrying X is joined to two other carbon atoms, e.g. 2-chloropropane (CH3)2CHCl and 2-chlorobutane CH3CHClCH2CH3.
Tertiary: the carbon carrying X is joined to three other carbon atoms, e.g. 2-chloro-2-methylpropane (CH3)3CCl.

blocks.alt: Top left: halothane drawn as two carbons, one with three F atoms and one with Cl, Br and H. Top right: mono-, di- and trihalogenoalkanes, a carbon with one, two or three X atoms. Bottom: chloroethane (primary), 2-chloropropane (secondary) and 2-chloro-2-methylpropane (tertiary).
blocks.caption: Halothane and the classes of halogenoalkanes (original diagram after the book's structures).
blocks.long_description: Halogenoalkanes are classed in two ways: by how many halogen atoms they contain, and, for monohalogenoalkanes, by how many carbon atoms are joined to the carbon that carries the halogen.

blocks.prompt: Give all the structures with formula C4H9Cl and classify each as primary, secondary or tertiary.

items: Halogenoalkane: alkane with H replaced by F, Cl, Br or I; R-X.
Primary, secondary, tertiary: the C carrying X has 1 (or 0), 2 or 3 C neighbours.
